transcript: Last night, I saw Walk On Through at MCC, written by and starring Gavin Creel. The show is basically a series of songs about experiences and ideas Gavin has while walking through the Metropolitan Museum of Art. Going into this, I knew Gavin Creel was a great singer, but I had no idea he was also a great writer and musician. The music was great, I really enjoyed it. Some other parts of the show I wasn't quite as jazzed about, mainly I wish it were a little more specific in what it was trying to say and do. It was partially about certain art pieces and partly about Gavin's relationship to them without being really married to one of these concepts more than the other. Overall, I left thinking mostly about how we use art to interpret ourselves and our lives — basically how we project. But I wanted it to be more personal to Gavin. I think this would have made it maybe more compelling to those who are not art enthusiasts. And I do get a sense from this show that Gavin does have an interesting relationship to art and paintings so I really wonder what this piece would have looked like had it not been originally commissioned by the MET. All that aside though, if you want to see Gavin Creel and a group of other very talented folks perform some great songs with great projection designs as a backdrop, you will not be disappointed. With that, another program for my collection.
